#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests for freq.py's corpus loaders.

Run: python3 keyboards/svalboard/test_freq.py

Only the loaders with a *parseable input format* are pinned here. `prompts`,
`shell` and `code` read whatever happens to be on this machine and have no
contract worth asserting; the Slack and Discord loaders read an export format
that is specified elsewhere and can silently change under us, which is exactly
the thing a test should catch.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import freq


class SlackLoaderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def with_dump(self, name: str, payload) -> Path:
        """Point freq.SLACK_DIR at a temp dir holding one dump file."""
        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        d = Path(tmp.name)
        (d / name).write_text(json.dumps(payload))
        old = freq.SLACK_DIR
        freq.SLACK_DIR = d
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))
        return d

    def test_slack_is_a_registered_source(self):
        self.assertIn("slack", freq.SOURCES)

    def test_yields_message_text_from_a_dump(self):
        self.with_dump("dump.json", [{"text": "one"}, {"text": "two"}])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["one", "two"])

    def test_missing_dump_dir_yields_nothing(self):
        old = freq.SLACK_DIR
        freq.SLACK_DIR = Path("/nonexistent/svalboard-freq-test/slack")
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), [])

    def test_html_entities_are_unescaped(self):
        # The layout argues about where `&` goes; Slack ships it as &, so
        # counting the raw text would undercount the character this repo cares
        # most about placing.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [{"text": "a & b <c> d"}])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["a & b <c> d"])

    def test_mentions_and_channel_refs_are_dropped(self):
        # You autocomplete these; your hands never type the U0123ABC.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "hey <@U0123ABC> see <#C0456DEF|general> <!here>"},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["hey  see  "])

    def test_links_keep_the_label_and_drop_the_url(self):
        # A pasted URL is not typing; a label you wrote is.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "see <https://ex.com/x|the docs> and <https://ex.com/y>"},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["see the docs and "])

    def test_subtyped_and_empty_messages_are_skipped(self):
        # Joins, bot posts and file-share stubs are not keystrokes.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "real"},
            {"text": "x joined", "subtype": "channel_join"},
            {"text": "beep", "subtype": "bot_message"},
            {"text": ""},
            {"no_text_key": 1},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["real"])

    def test_accepts_the_messages_envelope_form(self):
        # slack_search_* returns {"messages": [...]}; a hand-saved dump may be
        # the bare list. Both are dumps we would plausibly write.
        self.with_dump("d.json", {"messages": [{"text": "enveloped"}]})

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["enveloped"])


class DiscordLoaderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def with_export(self, *channels: tuple[str, str]) -> Path:
        """Point freq.DISCORD_DIR at a temp export root.

        Each channel is (dir_name, raw messages.csv text) -- raw, because the
        CSV quoting is half of what this loader has to get right.
        """
        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        root = Path(tmp.name)
        for name, csv_text in channels:
            d = root / "messages" / name
            d.mkdir(parents=True)
            (d / "messages.csv").write_text(csv_text)
        old = freq.DISCORD_DIR
        freq.DISCORD_DIR = root
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "DISCORD_DIR", old))
        return root

    def test_discord_is_a_registered_source(self):
        self.assertIn("discord", freq.SOURCES)

    def test_yields_contents_across_channels(self):
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,hello,\n2,t,there,\n'),
            ("c2", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n3,t,again,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["hello", "there", "again"])

    def test_missing_export_yields_nothing(self):
        old = freq.DISCORD_DIR
        freq.DISCORD_DIR = Path("/nonexistent/svalboard-freq-test/discord")
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "DISCORD_DIR", old))

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), [])

    def test_multiline_messages_survive_csv_quoting(self):
        # The reason this reads CSV properly instead of splitting on newlines:
        # a quoted Contents field spans lines, and naive splitting would shred
        # every multi-line message into fragments.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,"one\ntwo",\n'),
        )

        self.with_export((
            "c1",
            'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n'

        ))

        self.assertEqual(
            list(freq.iter_discord_text()),
            ["hey  and  in  role  emoji :party: :spin:"],
        )

    def test_empty_contents_rows_are_skipped(self):
        # Attachment-only messages: a drag-and-drop, not keystrokes.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,,https://cdn/x.png\n2,t,real,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["real"])

    def test_unexpected_columns_skip_the_file_without_crashing(self):
        # Discord has changed this export's shape before; a silent zero-count
        # is worse than a loud skip.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Body\n1,t,hello\n'),
            ("c2", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n2,t,fine,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["fine"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def aggregate_payload(corpus):
    """The committable half of a run: per-1000 rates, no corpus text.

    Sources that collected nothing are omitted rather than written out as a
    full table of 0.0. This file is the public evidence base the README's
    placement argument rests on, and a column of measured zeros is the
    strongest claim you can make about a character -- "you never type this" --
    where the truth is only "this was never measured". `discord` is exactly
    that until the export arrives.
    """
    every = [c for c in map(chr, range(33, 127)) if not c.isalnum()]
    agg = rates(corpus, every)
    present = [k for k in corpus if agg[k]["_chars"]]
    return {
        "generated_by": "freq.py",
        "note": "Per-1000-character rates. Aggregates only -- the corpus itself "
                "is local (~/.local/share/svalboard-freq) and unpublishable. "
                "A source absent here collected nothing; it is not a measured zero.",
        "corpus_chars": {k: agg[k]["_chars"] for k in present},
        "rates": {k: {c: round(agg[k][c], 4) for c in every} for k in present},
    }

6	reports per-1000-character rates -- so the next "should I promote X?" is one
7	command instead of a re-derivation.

10	    python3 freq.py '`' '~'        # rates for specific characters
11	    python3 freq.py --all          # every printable ASCII symbol

14	WHERE THE CORPUS LIVES, AND WHY NOT HERE

16	The cache goes in ~/.local/share/svalboard-freq/, never in this repo. This repo
17	is public; the corpus is shell history and prompts, which carry internal
18	hostnames, paths and work detail. What IS safe to commit is the aggregate --

20	writes freq.json here and that is what the README's table is built from.

23	the manifest records the filters that produced it, but not their intent.

26	-----------

28	           machine-injected blocks are dropped -- see EXCLUDE_PREFIXES. What
29	           survives is meant to be keystrokes your hands actually made, which

38	           iter_slack_text) and this reads them.

1	## Objective
2	
3	Wire Sauyon's own typing corpus into `jeffzi/svalboard_layout_optimizer` and run it over the
4	Svalboard layer-0 alphas + the 7 promoted symbols (thumbs frozen), reporting the delta against
5	the current layout rather than a bare winner.

8	candidate, and the delta is dominated by two metrics that encode the same editorial opinion
9	twice. Review: **incomplete** — two of four angles never delivered (tooling, not findings).
10	
11	## State
12	
13	Committed on `master`, ahead of `origin/master` by 2 (**not pushed** — see Next step):
14

21	unchanged.

24	edited (new `BuildNgramsTests`, `KeyboardConfigTests`, `keyboard_config()`), and two commits I
25	did not author appeared under Sauyon's name with an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Nothing was
26	lost and everything passes, but the single-writer assumption did not hold — verify the tree is
27	what you expect before building on it.

30	
31	`freq.py` now builds five corpora. Sizes, and the per-1000 rates are in the committed
32	`freq.json` (aggregates only — the corpus itself stayed in `~/.local/share/svalboard-freq/`):
33	
34	| corpus | chars | note |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| prompts | 6,592,073 | |
37	| code | 641,649 | |
38	| shell | 400,634 | |
39	| slack | 15,179 | 240 messages, 12 of 20 search pages — **thin, see Open questions** |
40	| discord | 0 | export not requested yet |

43	`~/.local/share/svalboard-freq/slack/search-from-me-2026-09-01.json`. Two of fourteen pages
44	were refused by the permission classifier; the sample is what got through, not a designed cut.

46	### The result
47	
48	One `optimize_sa` run, one start layout (the current one), `--fix ",./;\"'"`:
49	
50	```
51	current    w□r-xf~s@cm(nvlpgtbd.,a:uq/e)o";i&y'zhjk    cost 1035.60
52	candidate  □juhyv~pkdxfswbgmt:l.,n(r&/eoa";c@)'ziq-    cost  216.03
53	```
54	
55	**Do not read that as 4.8× better.** The gap is concentrated in four metrics:
56	
57	| metric | current | candidate |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| Character Constraints | 445.82 | 83.63 |
60	| FSB (full scissor) | 267.37 | 0.84 |
61	| SFB | 226.93 | 78.19 |
62	| Manual Bigram Penalty | 47.06 | 6.08 |
63	
64	**The finding worth having is what drives Character Constraints and Manual Bigram Penalty.**
65	Both are weight `1000.0` in `config/evaluation/sval.yml`, and both encode *the same rule*:
66	a key you press twice in a row does not belong on a pinky or ring lateral. `character_constraints`
67	lists `l s t f p r m c n , . ' - ?` with cost 10 on those positions; `manual_bigram_penalty`
68	charges 10 for a same-key repeat there against 1 on center/south.
69	
70	The current layout puts **`-` on the left pinky East** — matrix `[3, 2]`, the 10-cost position in
71	*both*. `-` is 46.6% of the current layout's Character Constraints penalty, and `--` is 92.3% of
72	its Manual Bigram Penalty. In Sauyon's corpus `-` runs 44.30/1k in shell, overwhelmingly as
73	`--flag`.
74	
75	That is a real argument against the README, and the README half-made it itself: it justifies `~`
76	on a ring lateral by counting repeat-runs ("338 occurrences hand-typed, **zero** of them
77	consecutive repeats"). It never ran that test on `-`. **`-` fails the README's own test**, and
78	the optimizer found it.
79	
80	Caveat that keeps this honest: one opinion applied through two metrics is not two independent
81	confirmations, and it is ~48% of the cost gap. FSB (267 → 0.84) is a separate and larger effect
82	that nobody has audited yet.
83	
84	## Decisions + rationale
85	
86	1. **Two scope assumptions from the scope phase were overturned; both were cheap.**
87	   - *"33 glyphs over 40 switches, 7 free."* Wrong: 6 of those 7 hold frequent punctuation
88	     (`, . / ; " '`) and only `tab` is glyph-less. All 40 finger keys are `fixed_keys: false`,
89	     so freezing the 6 needs `--fix`, which `optimize_sa` supports ("do not optimize those
90	     keys"). `tab` becomes the one `□`.
91	   - *"`ngram_merge.rs` probably does the weighted blend."* It does, exactly — each component is
92	     rescaled to the first's total, then multiplied by its weight. Nothing hand-rolled.
93	
94	2. **Thumbs are frozen by the config, not by us.** `sval.yml` marks all twelve thumb switches
95	   `fixed_keys: true`, so they are not in the 40-char layout string at all. The non-negotiable
96	   holds by construction.
97	
98	3. **A derived keyboard config was necessary and is the one edit to optimizer config.**
99	   `optimize_sa` rejects any glyph absent from `base_layout`'s first level, and the stock
100	   `sval.yml` carries the author's own Hands Down variant with no `" & ( ) / : ; @ ~`. Running
101	   Sauyon's layer 0 against it dies with *"Unsupported characters in provided layout"*.
102	   `optimize.keyboard_config()` rewrites **only** the glyph inventory into
103	   `config/keyboard/sauyon_sval.yml`; `positions` and `key_costs` are copied untouched, because
104	   the scope phase forbade re-measuring geometry the costs were fitted to. Tests pin that the
105	   costs and thumb block are byte-identical.
106	
107	4. **`freq.py` still has no network.** The Slack fetch is a separate step that writes JSON dumps
108	   into `$CACHE/slack/`; the loader only parses them. Credentials and the `from:@me` scope
109	   decision stay out of a frequency counter.
110	
111	5. **Corpus weights are the softest number here** and are one editable constant:
112	   `prompts .40 / shell .20 / code .20 / slack .15 / discord .05`. They are estimated shares of a
113	   day's typing, **not** corpus sizes — prompts is 430× the Slack sample and nobody types in
114	   that ratio. Any result should be re-run against a different guess before it is believed.
115	
116	## Interfaces / contracts
117	
118	```
119	keyboards/svalboard/freq.py
120	  SOURCES = {prompts, shell, code, slack, discord}   # each a generator yielding str
121	  SLACK_DIR   = $CACHE/slack        *.json, bare list or {"messages":[...]}, skips `subtype`
122	  DISCORD_DIR = $CACHE/discord      unzipped export; messages/<channel>/messages.csv
123	  slack_plain(text)     strips <@U…>/<#C…>/<!…> and bare <url>, keeps <url|label> labels,
124	                        then unescapes < > & (in that order)
125	  discord_plain(text)   strips <@123>/<#123>/<@&123>, reduces <:name:123> -> :name:
126	
127	keyboards/svalboard/optimize.py
128	  layout_string()       -> 40 chars, cup order N W C E S, cups L pinky..L index, R index..R pinky
129	                           read from build.build_layers()[0] via cheatsheet.label()
130	  PERMUTING             26 alphas + "-:()&@~"          FIXED  ",./;\"'"   (passed as --fix)
131	  WEIGHTS               per-corpus blend shares
132	  checked_name(name)    rejects separators/".."/"" before the name reaches shutil.rmtree
133	  keyboard_config(yml, layout) -> derived yml with only the glyph inventory replaced
134	  strip_path_markers()  removes iter_code_text's "\x00PATH:<rel>\n" headers
135	
136	  python3 optimize.py --opt <checkout> [--ngrams-only | --evaluate-only] [--name NAME]
137	
138	optimizer contract (learned, unchanged)
139	  ngrams <corpus.txt> <outdir>            -> {1,2,3}-grams.txt, "<weight> <ngram>"
140	  ngram_merge <outdir> dir:w [dir:w ...]  -> weighted blend, first component sets the level
141	  scripts/ngrams/normalize.py <dir>       -> percentages, newline-bearing ngrams excluded
142	```
143	
144	## Open questions

147	   - *iteration 1* — security + error-handling delivered (3 nits, below). correctness and
148	     type-design finished without ever calling `submit_findings`.

164	     Rated a nit; it is worse than that — it strands raw work Slack and shell history inside the

6. **Correctness was reviewed by an in-harness read-only agent, not by the drovr panel.**
   Recorded because it is a deviation. Panel history: iteration 1 delivered security +
   type-design + error-handling but correctness never called `submit_findings`; iteration 2
   delivered security + error-handling **clean against the current tree**, correctness and
   type-design timed out; iterations 3 and 4 failed to seed at all — *"the seed was NOT
   delivered — herdr saw no state change… Read the pane, clear whatever is on it"*, which needs
   a human at a tmux pane. After four attempts I dispatched a read-only `Explore` agent for the
   correctness angle rather than ship unreviewed. It stayed read-only, so single-writer held.
   **It was the most productive reviewer of the four** — its three Important findings are all
   fixed in `a7c4a90`.

7. **Corpus weights are the softest number in the pipeline** and sit in one editable constant:
   `prompts .40 / shell .20 / code .20 / slack .15 / discord .05`. They are estimated shares of a
   day's typing, **not** corpus sizes — prompts is 430× the Slack sample and nobody types in that
   ratio. `discord` is dropped at run time while empty, so the live blend sums to 0.95; harmless,
   because `normalize.py` converts to percentages afterwards.

## Interfaces / contracts

```
keyboards/svalboard/freq.py
  SOURCES = {prompts, shell, code, slack, discord}   # each a generator yielding str
  SLACK_DIR   = $CACHE/slack        *.json, bare list or {"messages":[...]}, skips `subtype`
  DISCORD_DIR = $CACHE/discord      unzipped export; messages/<channel>/messages.csv
  slack_plain(text)      strips <@U…>/<#C…>/<!…> and bare <url>, keeps <url|label> labels,
                         then unescapes < > & -- & LAST, and that order is pinned
                         by a test: reversed, a typed "<" collapses to "<"
  discord_plain(text)    strips <@123>/<#123>/<@&123>, reduces <:name:123> -> :name:
  aggregate_payload(corpus) -> the freq.json dict; omits sources whose corpus is empty

keyboards/svalboard/optimize.py
  layout_string()        -> 40 chars, cup order N W C E S, cups L pinky..L index, R index..R pinky
                            read from build.build_layers()[0] via cheatsheet.label()
  PERMUTING              26 alphas + "-:()&@~"        FIXED  ",./;\"'"  (passed as --fix)
  WEIGHTS                per-corpus blend shares
  checked_name(name)     rejects separators/".."/"" before the name reaches shutil.rmtree
  keyboard_config(yml, layout) -> derived yml, glyph inventory replaced and nothing else
  build_ngrams(opt, corpus_dir, name, prefix)  -> ngrams/<prefix>_<name>, or None if empty
  strip_path_markers()   removes iter_code_text's "\x00PATH:<rel>\n" headers

  python3 optimize.py --opt <checkout> [--ngrams-only | --evaluate-only] [--name NAME]

optimizer contract (learned this phase, unchanged by us)
  ngrams <corpus.txt> <outdir>            -> {1,2,3}-grams.txt, lines "<weight> <ngram>"
  ngram_merge <outdir> dir:w [dir:w ...]  -> weighted blend, first component sets the level
  scripts/ngrams/normalize.py <dir>       -> percentages, newline-bearing ngrams excluded
  optimize_sa --fix '<chars>'             -> "do not optimize those keys"; verified it holds
  NOTE: go-task is NOT installed here. optimize.py drives cargo directly, mirroring Taskfile.yml.
```

1. **Deferred review findings, recorded rather than fixed.** All rated nit; quoted so nobody
   meets them as bugs:
   - *"`SLACK_LINK_BARE` deletes typed angle-bracket text on any dump that isn't API-escaped:
     `slack_plain("Vec<String> is fine")` → `"Vec is fine"`."* Correct for the search/history
     output we actually feed it, wrong for a hand-assembled dump. **Not fixed** — the two cases
     are genuinely ambiguous in the wire format, and the real dumps are escaped. Revisit if
     anyone hand-writes a dump.
   - *"`iter_slack_text` claims 'messages you sent' but applies no author filter."* True; the
     convention is enforced by the `from:@me` query at fetch time and by the filename. **Not
     fixed** — a filter needs a configured user id that nothing else needs.
   - *"`discord_plain` does not handle `<t:1700000000:R>` timestamps … contributing two `:` per
     timestamp"*, and `:` is a promoted symbol. **Not fixed, but this one is worth fixing** the
     moment a real export lands, because it biases exactly the character it touches.
   - *"`--name eng_wiki_1m` passes the regex and deletes the optimizer's shipped corpus."*
     `checked_name` blocks path escapes, not collisions. **Not fixed** — the checkout is
     ephemeral and re-fetchable.
   - *"`--append-solutions-to` appends across invocations and nothing truncates."* Deliberate:
     it is what let four restarts accumulate into one comparison table. Everything is re-scored
     under the current config, so stale rows cannot skew the delta.

2. **Is FSB 267 → 0.84 real?** It is the single largest component of the gap and nothing in this
   phase audited it. The current layout's worst offenders are `pl` (42.3%), `mc`, `md`. Read
   `config/evaluation/sval.yml`'s scissor definition and confirm before believing it. If FSB is

3. **The Slack sample is thin** — 15k chars against shell's 400k — yet carries a 0.15 blend
   weight. Fine for unigram rates, weak for trigrams. Either pull more pages (the search
   paginates 20 at a time; cursors are `base64("CURRENT_PAGE:<n>")`) or cut the weight to match

4. **Discord has not been requested, and it takes days to a month.** The loader is written and
   tested against the documented `messages/*/messages.csv` shape but has never seen a real

## Objective

Wire Sauyon's own typing corpus into `jeffzi/svalboard_layout_optimizer` and run it over the
Svalboard layer-0 alphas + the 7 promoted symbols (thumbs frozen), reporting the delta against
the current layout rather than a bare winner.

Code: **done, reviewed, committed and pushed.** Run: **done**, four annealing restarts.
Review: **all four angles covered**, but only after the drovr panel failed four times and the
correctness angle had to be dispatched a different way (Decisions 6).

The headline is not a layout. It is one sentence: **`-` fails the README's own test, and the
README never ran it.**

## State

`master` at `a7c4a90`, **pushed** to `forge.ko.ag`, working tree clean. `09bc424..a7c4a90`:

- `86df2a6` measure the layout against the corpus that is actually typed
- `394dc86` don't strand corpus text in the optimizer checkout on a failed build
- `852ab6f` derive the optimizer's keyboard config instead of borrowing its glyphs
- `a7c4a90` stop publishing a source that measured nothing as measured zeros

**40 tests pass, none skipped** (`python3 test_freq.py` 18, `python3 test_optimize.py` 22).
`python3 build.py` passes all four guards (32 geometry assertions against the hardware,
26 letters + 10 digits, 110 keycodes) and regenerates `SvalHandsDownNeu.vil` byte-identical.

⚠️ **A second writer was active in this tree during the phase.** Files reappeared edited between
my writes (the `CorpusNameTests`/`KeyboardConfigTests` classes, and a `checked_name` I then found
duplicated), and this handoff already existed when I went to author it — I merged rather than
discarded. Nothing was lost and everything passes, but the single-writer assumption did not
hold. Check `git log` before building on this.

### The corpus

`freq.py` now builds five corpora; `freq.json` (committed, aggregates only) reports four,
because a source that collected nothing is now omitted rather than published as measured zeros:

| corpus | chars | note |
|---|---|---|
| prompts | 6,592,073 | |
| code | 641,649 | |
| shell | 400,634 | |
| slack | 15,179 | 240 messages — **thin, see Open questions 3** |
| discord | 0 | export not requested yet; omitted from `freq.json` |

Slack came from the Slack MCP `from:<@U0A9ZHCGHDJ>` search, 12 of 14 attempted pages (two were
refused by the permission classifier), dumped to
`~/.local/share/svalboard-freq/slack/search-from-me-2026-09-01.json`. The sample is what got
through, not a designed cut.

### The result — four restarts, not one

```
current     w□r-xf~s@cm(nvlpgtbd.,a:uq/e)o";i&y'zhjk    cost 1035.60
run 4       zvukwd@pjt)mn:hfbsxc.,r(l&/oqa";g□e'yi~-    cost  146.37
run 3       □qrhxg~tvdj&akywmn:l.,e(o)/pfu";s@c'biz-    cost  210.42
run 2       □jtzkxqsvfwycgdhmn:l.,p)r&/e(a";b-o'~u@i    cost  210.63
run 1       □juhyv~pkdxfswbgmt:l.,n(r&/eoa";c@)'ziq-    cost  216.03
```

**No candidate here is actionable and none should be typed.** They agree with the current layout
on only **7–10 of 40 keys**, and they do not agree with *each other* — three cluster at ~210 and
one sits at 146, from identical inputs. The metric landscape has many near-equal basins, so
"the winner" is largely an artifact of a random seed.

What *is* stable across all four independent runs is the direction:

| char | current | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | run 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-` | **L pinky E** | R pinky S | R ring E | R pinky S | R pinky S |
| `:` | R index E | L index E | L index E | L index E | L middle E |
| `(` | L middle W | R index E | R middle E | R index E | R index E |

**Every run moves `-` off the left pinky lateral, and every run moves it to the other hand.**

### Why — and this is the finding

The gap is concentrated in four metrics (current → run 1):

| metric | current | candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Character Constraints | 445.82 | 83.63 |
| FSB (full scissor) | 267.37 | 0.84 |
| SFB | 226.93 | 78.19 |
| Manual Bigram Penalty | 47.06 | 6.08 |

`character_constraints` and `manual_bigram_penalty` are both weight `1000.0` in
`config/evaluation/sval.yml` and both encode one rule: **a key you press twice in a row does not
belong on a pinky or ring lateral.** `-` sits on the left pinky East, matrix `[3, 2]`, the
10-cost position in both. It is 46.6% of the current layout's Character Constraints penalty, and
`--` is 92.3% of its Manual Bigram Penalty.

The README already invented this test — for a different character. It justifies `~` on a ring
lateral by counting repeat-runs: *"338 occurrences hand-typed, **zero** of them consecutive
repeats, longest run 1. … a key you never hit twice in a row is the right thing to put somewhere
awkward."* It never ran that count on `-`.

I ran it, over the blended corpus (`ngrams/sauyon/2-grams.txt` against `1-grams.txt`):

| char | unigram % | `xx` bigram % | share of presses that are a double |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`-`** | 1.842 | 0.3718 | **40.4%** |
| `l` | 2.917 | 0.3199 | 21.9% |
| `p` | 1.760 | 0.1109 | 12.6% |
| `f` | 1.369 | 0.0752 | 11.0% |
| `s` | 4.455 | 0.1999 | 9.0% |
| `o` | 5.232 | 0.1608 | 6.1% |
| `e` | 8.140 | 0.1603 | 3.9% |
| `a` | 4.736 | 0.0035 | 0.1% |

**`-` is doubled more than any other character on the board — nearly twice the next worst.**
`--flag` is why. The README promoted `-` to the left pinky East on raw frequency ("the clear
winner on both counts", 44.30/1k in shell) and, by its own `~` argument, that is the wrong
number to have used: two in five `-` presses are the second half of a `--`, on a pinky lateral.

That argument stands on its own and does not depend on trusting the optimizer's cost function.

**Caveat, stated plainly:** one editorial opinion applied through two metrics is not two
independent confirmations, and those two are ~48% of the cost gap. FSB (267 → 0.84) is a
separate and larger effect that **nobody has audited** — see Open questions 2.

## Decisions + rationale

1. **Both scope-phase assumptions were overturned, both cheaply.**
   - *"33 glyphs over 40 switches, 7 free."* Wrong: 6 of those 7 hold frequent punctuation
     (`, . / ; " '`) and only `tab` is glyph-less. All 40 finger keys are `fixed_keys: false`,
     so freezing the 6 needs `--fix`, which `optimize_sa` supports ("do not optimize those
     keys"). Verified it held: all six stayed at indices 20, 21, 26, 30, 31, 35 in every run.
   - *"`ngram_merge.rs` probably does the weighted blend."* It does, exactly — each component is
     rescaled to the first's total, then multiplied by its weight. Nothing was hand-rolled.

2. **Thumbs are frozen by the config, not by us.** `sval.yml` marks all twelve thumb switches
   `fixed_keys: true`, so they are not in the 40-char layout string at all. The non-negotiable
   holds by construction, not by our discipline.

3. **A derived keyboard config was necessary, and is the only optimizer config we touch.**
   `optimize_sa` rejects any glyph absent from `base_layout`'s first level, and the stock
   `sval.yml` carries the optimizer author's own Hands Down variant with no `" & ( ) / : ; @ ~`.
   Sauyon's layer 0 died on it: *"Unsupported characters in provided layout: '"&()/:;@~'"*.
   `keyboard_config()` rewrites **only** the glyph inventory, into
   `config/keyboard/sauyon_sval.yml` inside the ephemeral checkout. `positions` and `key_costs`
   are copied untouched — the scope phase forbade re-measuring geometry the costs were fitted
   to, and this respects that. Tests pin that the costs and thumb block come through unchanged.

4. **The cup-order mapping was verified end to end, not just by our own tests.** The optimizer's
   renderer draws layer 0 back from the string we hand it, and it matches README.md's table key
   for key. That is an independent check no test in this repo could give, because both `build.py`
   and the README live here. Reproduce with `optimize.py --evaluate-only`.

5. **`freq.py` still has no network.** The Slack fetch is a separate step that writes JSON dumps
   into `$CACHE/slack/`; the loader only parses them. Credentials and the `from:@me` scope
   decision stay out of a frequency counter, and the loader stays testable.

6. **Correctness was reviewed by an in-harness read-only agent, not by the drovr panel.**
   Recorded because it is a deviation. Panel history: iteration 1 delivered security,
   type-design and error-handling, but correctness finished without ever calling
   `submit_findings`; iteration 2 delivered security + error-handling **clean against the
   current tree**, correctness and type-design timed out; iterations 3 and 4 failed to seed at
   all — *"the seed was NOT delivered — herdr saw no state change… Read the pane, clear whatever
   is on it"*, which needs a human at a tmux pane. After four attempts I dispatched a read-only
   `Explore` agent for the correctness angle rather than ship unreviewed. It wrote nothing, so
   single-writer held. **It was the most productive reviewer of the four** — its three Important
   findings are all fixed in `a7c4a90`:
   - *"a source that collected nothing is published as a full table of measured zeros"* — `discord`
     appeared in the public `freq.json` as 94 symbols at 0.0 next to `corpus_chars: 0`.
   - *"`test_the_real_config_takes_the_real_layout` can never fail"* — skipped on a missing
     fixture and had no assertions anyway, while being the only test claiming to cover the
     cup-order property.
   - *"the `&`-last ordering … is not pinned by any test"* — reversing it turns a typed
     `<` into `<`, four keystrokes counted as one, one of them the `&` whose rate the README
     uses to place it.

7. **Corpus weights are the softest number in the pipeline** and sit in one editable constant:
   `prompts .40 / shell .20 / code .20 / slack .15 / discord .05`. They are estimated shares of a
   day's typing, **not** corpus sizes — prompts is 430× the Slack sample and nobody types in that
   ratio. `discord` is dropped at run time while empty, so the live blend sums to 0.95; harmless,
   because `normalize.py` converts to percentages afterwards.

Phase done. All 5 checklist steps complete.

## The finding

**`-` fails the README's own test, and the README never ran it.**

The README puts `-` on the left pinky East from raw frequency ("the clear winner on both counts", 44.30/1k in shell). Three bullets later it argues `~` onto a ring lateral on a *different* basis — repeat-runs: *"338 occurrences, zero of them consecutive repeats… a key you never hit twice in a row is the right thing to put somewhere awkward."*

I ran that count on `-`:

| char | share of presses that are a double |
|---|---|
| **`-`** | **40.4%** |
| `l` | 21.9% |
| `p` | 12.6% |
| `f` | 11.0% |

`-` is doubled more than anything else on the board, nearly 2× the next worst — `--flag`. And it sits on a pinky lateral, the exact position the optimizer's two weight-1000 metrics forbid for repeated keys. All four independent search runs move it off that key and onto the right hand.

## The delta

Current layout costs **1035.60**. Four annealing restarts: 146.37, 210.42, 210.63, 216.03 — but they share only **7–10 of 40 keys** with the current layout *and disagree with each other*. **Don't adopt any of them**; that spread is a random seed talking. The stable signal is directional, not a layout.

Honest caveat: ~48% of the gap comes from two metrics encoding one editorial opinion, so it's not two confirmations. FSB (267 → 0.84) is larger still and **nobody has audited it** — that's the top open question.

## Shipped

4 commits pushed, `09bc424..a7c4a90`. `freq.py` gained `slack` (JSON dumps; no network in the counter) and `discord` (official export, not an API scrape). `optimize.py` is the corpus→ngram→search bridge. **40 tests, 0 skipped**; `build.py`'s four guards pass and the `.vil` is byte-identical. Thumbs never moved — `sval.yml` marks them `fixed_keys`, so it holds by construction.

Two things you should know:

1. **The drovr code-review panel is broken here.** Four dispatches; two died with *"the seed was NOT delivered"* and want a human to `drovr attach` and clear the pane. Correctness never delivered in any iteration, so I dispatched a read-only in-harness reviewer instead — a deviation, recorded in the handoff. It was the most productive of the four: 3 Important findings, all fixed. One was that `freq.json` published `discord` as 94 measured zeros in a public repo.
2. **A second session was writing this tree throughout** — files reappeared edited, and the handoff already existed when I went to write it (I merged rather than discarded). Two panel failures were "HEAD moved since the iteration was seeded" because of it.

**Next action, under two minutes:** request the Discord export — Settings → Data & Privacy → Request all my data. It takes days to a month and the loader is written and tested but has never seen a real one. Everything else here can wait; that clock can't be started retroactively.

48	`~/.local/share/svalboard-freq/slack/search-from-me-2026-09-01.json`. The sample is what got
49	through, not a designed cut.
50	
51	### The result — four restarts, not one
52	
53	```
54	current     w□r-xf~s@cm(nvlpgtbd.,a:uq/e)o";i&y'zhjk    cost 1035.60
55	run 4       zvukwd@pjt)mn:hfbsxc.,r(l&/oqa";g□e'yi~-    cost  146.37
56	run 3       □qrhxg~tvdj&akywmn:l.,e(o)/pfu";s@c'biz-    cost  210.42
57	run 2       □jtzkxqsvfwycgdhmn:l.,p)r&/e(a";b-o'~u@i    cost  210.63
58	run 1       □juhyv~pkdxfswbgmt:l.,n(r&/eoa";c@)'ziq-    cost  216.03
59	```
60	
61	**No candidate here is actionable and none should be typed.** They agree with the current layout
62	on only **7–10 of 40 keys**, and they do not agree with *each other* — three cluster at ~210 and
63	one sits at 146, from identical inputs. The metric landscape has many near-equal basins, so
64	"the winner" is largely an artifact of a random seed.
65	
66	What *is* stable across all four independent runs is the direction:
67	
68	| char | current | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | run 4 |
69	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
70	| `-` | **L pinky E** | R pinky S | R ring E | R pinky S | R pinky S |
71	| `:` | R index E | L index E | L index E | L index E | L middle E |
72	| `(` | L middle W | R index E | R middle E | R index E | R index E |
73	
74	**Every run moves `-` off the left pinky lateral, and every run moves it to the other hand.**
75	
76	### Why — and this is the finding
77	
78	The gap is concentrated in four metrics (current → run 1):
79	
80	| metric | current | candidate |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| Character Constraints | 445.82 | 83.63 |
83	| FSB (full scissor) | 267.37 | 0.84 |
84	| SFB | 226.93 | 78.19 |
85	| Manual Bigram Penalty | 47.06 | 6.08 |
86	
87	`character_constraints` and `manual_bigram_penalty` are both weight `1000.0` in
88	`config/evaluation/sval.yml` and both encode one rule: **a key you press twice in a row does not
89	belong on a pinky or ring lateral.** `-` sits on the left pinky East, matrix `[3, 2]`, the
90	10-cost position in both. It is 46.6% of the current layout's Character Constraints penalty, and
91	`--` is 92.3% of its Manual Bigram Penalty.
92	
93	The README already invented this test — for a different character. It justifies `~` on a ring
94	lateral by counting repeat-runs: *"338 occurrences hand-typed, **zero** of them consecutive
95	repeats, longest run 1. … a key you never hit twice in a row is the right thing to put somewhere
96	awkward."* It never ran that count on `-`.
97	
98	I ran it, over the blended corpus (`ngrams/sauyon/2-grams.txt` against `1-grams.txt`):
99	
100	| char | unigram % | `xx` bigram % | share of presses that are a double |
101	|---|---|---|---|
102	| **`-`** | 1.842 | 0.3718 | **40.4%** |
103	| `l` | 2.917 | 0.3199 | 21.9% |
104	| `p` | 1.760 | 0.1109 | 12.6% |
105	| `f` | 1.369 | 0.0752 | 11.0% |
106	| `s` | 4.455 | 0.1999 | 9.0% |
107	| `o` | 5.232 | 0.1608 | 6.1% |
108	| `e` | 8.140 | 0.1603 | 3.9% |
109	| `a` | 4.736 | 0.0035 | 0.1% |
110	
111	**`-` is doubled more than any other character on the board — nearly twice the next worst.**
112	`--flag` is why. The README promoted `-` to the left pinky East on raw frequency ("the clear
113	winner on both counts", 44.30/1k in shell) and, by its own `~` argument, that is the wrong
114	number to have used: two in five `-` presses are the second half of a `--`, on a pinky lateral.
115	
116	That argument stands on its own and does not depend on trusting the optimizer's cost function.
117	
118	**Caveat, stated plainly:** one editorial opinion applied through two metrics is not two
119	independent confirmations, and those two are ~48% of the cost gap. FSB (267 → 0.84) is a
120	separate and larger effect that **nobody has audited** — see Open questions 2.
121	
122	## Decisions + rationale
123	
124	1. **Both scope-phase assumptions were overturned, both cheaply.**
125	   - *"33 glyphs over 40 switches, 7 free."* Wrong: 6 of those 7 hold frequent punctuation
126	     (`, . / ; " '`) and only `tab` is glyph-less. All 40 finger keys are `fixed_keys: false`,
127	     so freezing the 6 needs `--fix`, which `optimize_sa` supports ("do not optimize those
128	     keys"). Verified it held: all six stayed at indices 20, 21, 26, 30, 31, 35 in every run.
129	   - *"`ngram_merge.rs` probably does the weighted blend."* It does, exactly — each component is
130	     rescaled to the first's total, then multiplied by its weight. Nothing was hand-rolled.
131	
132	2. **Thumbs are frozen by the config, not by us.** `sval.yml` marks all twelve thumb switches
133	   `fixed_keys: true`, so they are not in the 40-char layout string at all. The non-negotiable
134	   holds by construction, not by our discipline.
135	
136	3. **A derived keyboard config was necessary, and is the only optimizer config we touch.**
137	   `optimize_sa` rejects any glyph absent from `base_layout`'s first level, and the stock
138	   `sval.yml` carries the optimizer author's own Hands Down variant with no `" & ( ) / : ; @ ~`.
139	   Sauyon's layer 0 died on it: *"Unsupported characters in provided layout: '"&()/:;@~'"*.
140	   `keyboard_config()` rewrites **only** the glyph inventory, into
141	   `config/keyboard/sauyon_sval.yml` inside the ephemeral checkout. `positions` and `key_costs`
142	   are copied untouched — the scope phase forbade re-measuring geometry the costs were fitted
143	   to, and this respects that. Tests pin that the costs and thumb block come through unchanged.
144	
145	4. **The cup-order mapping was verified end to end, not just by our own tests.** The optimizer's
146	   renderer draws layer 0 back from the string we hand it, and it matches README.md's table key

"""Tests for freq.py's corpus loaders.

Run: python3 keyboards/svalboard/test_freq.py

Only the loaders with a *parseable input format* are pinned here. `prompts`,
`shell` and `code` read whatever happens to be on this machine and have no
contract worth asserting; the Slack and Discord loaders read an export format
that is specified elsewhere and can silently change under us, which is exactly
the thing a test should catch.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import freq


class SlackLoaderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def with_dump(self, name: str, payload) -> Path:
        """Point freq.SLACK_DIR at a temp dir holding one dump file."""
        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        d = Path(tmp.name)
        (d / name).write_text(json.dumps(payload))
        old = freq.SLACK_DIR
        freq.SLACK_DIR = d
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))
        return d

    def test_slack_is_a_registered_source(self):
        self.assertIn("slack", freq.SOURCES)

    def test_yields_message_text_from_a_dump(self):
        self.with_dump("dump.json", [{"text": "one"}, {"text": "two"}])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["one", "two"])

    def test_missing_dump_dir_yields_nothing(self):
        old = freq.SLACK_DIR
        freq.SLACK_DIR = Path("/nonexistent/svalboard-freq-test/slack")
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), [])

    def test_html_entities_are_unescaped(self):
        # The layout argues about where `&` goes; Slack ships it as &, so
        # counting the raw text would undercount the character this repo cares
        # most about placing.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [{"text": "a & b <c> d"}])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["a & b <c> d"])

    def test_a_literally_typed_entity_survives_unescaping(self):
        # The reason slack_plain unescapes & LAST. Someone typing the four
        # characters "<" sends the wire form "&lt;". Unescape &
        # first and that collapses to "<": four keystrokes counted as one, and
        # one of them is the `&` whose rate decides where `&` goes.
        self.assertEqual(freq.slack_plain("&lt;"), "<")

    def test_mentions_and_channel_refs_are_dropped(self):
        # You autocomplete these; your hands never type the U0123ABC.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "hey <@U0123ABC> see <#C0456DEF|general> <!here>"},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["hey  see  "])

    def test_links_keep_the_label_and_drop_the_url(self):
        # A pasted URL is not typing; a label you wrote is.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "see <https://ex.com/x|the docs> and <https://ex.com/y>"},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["see the docs and "])

    def test_subtyped_and_empty_messages_are_skipped(self):
        # Joins, bot posts and file-share stubs are not keystrokes.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "real"},
            {"text": "x joined", "subtype": "channel_join"},
            {"text": "beep", "subtype": "bot_message"},
            {"text": ""},
            {"no_text_key": 1},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["real"])

    def test_accepts_the_messages_envelope_form(self):
        # slack_search_* returns {"messages": [...]}; a hand-saved dump may be
        # the bare list. Both are dumps we would plausibly write.
        self.with_dump("d.json", {"messages": [{"text": "enveloped"}]})

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["enveloped"])


class DiscordLoaderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def with_export(self, *channels: tuple[str, str]) -> Path:
        """Point freq.DISCORD_DIR at a temp export root.

        Each channel is (dir_name, raw messages.csv text) -- raw, because the
        CSV quoting is half of what this loader has to get right.
        """
        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        root = Path(tmp.name)
        for name, csv_text in channels:
            d = root / "messages" / name
            d.mkdir(parents=True)
            (d / "messages.csv").write_text(csv_text)
        old = freq.DISCORD_DIR
        freq.DISCORD_DIR = root
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "DISCORD_DIR", old))
        return root

    def test_discord_is_a_registered_source(self):
        self.assertIn("discord", freq.SOURCES)

    def test_yields_contents_across_channels(self):
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,hello,\n2,t,there,\n'),
            ("c2", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n3,t,again,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["hello", "there", "again"])

    def test_missing_export_yields_nothing(self):
        old = freq.DISCORD_DIR
        freq.DISCORD_DIR = Path("/nonexistent/svalboard-freq-test/discord")
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "DISCORD_DIR", old))

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), [])

    def test_multiline_messages_survive_csv_quoting(self):
        # The reason this reads CSV properly instead of splitting on newlines:
        # a quoted Contents field spans lines, and naive splitting would shred
        # every multi-line message into fragments.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,"one\ntwo",\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["one\ntwo"])

    def test_mentions_dropped_and_custom_emoji_reduced_to_typed_form(self):
        self.with_export((
            "c1",
            'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n'
            '1,t,"hey <@123> and <@!456> in <#789> role <@&321> emoji <:party:1> <a:spin:2>",\n',
        ))

        self.assertEqual(
            list(freq.iter_discord_text()),
            ["hey  and  in  role  emoji :party: :spin:"],
        )

    def test_empty_contents_rows_are_skipped(self):
        # Attachment-only messages: a drag-and-drop, not keystrokes.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,,https://cdn/x.png\n2,t,real,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["real"])

    def test_unexpected_columns_skip_the_file_without_crashing(self):
        # Discord has changed this export's shape before; a silent zero-count
        # is worse than a loud skip.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Body\n1,t,hello\n'),
            ("c2", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n2,t,fine,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["fine"])


class AggregateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_source_that_collected_nothing_is_omitted_not_zero_filled(self):
        # freq.json is the public evidence base the README's placement argument
        # rests on. A source with no corpus emitted as a full table of 0.0
        # reads as "measured, never typed" -- the strongest possible claim --
        # when it means "never measured". discord is exactly this until the
        # export lands.
        payload = freq.aggregate_payload({"shell": "abc", "discord": ""})

        self.assertEqual(set(payload["corpus_chars"]), {"shell"})
        self.assertEqual(set(payload["rates"]), {"shell"})

        payload = freq.aggregate_payload({"shell": "a-b-c"})

        self.assertEqual(payload["corpus_chars"]["shell"], 5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(payload["rates"]["shell"]["-"], 400.0)

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Run jeffzi/svalboard_layout_optimizer over the corpus freq.py collects.
3	
4	    python3 optimize.py --opt ~/src/svalboard_layout_optimizer          # full run
5	    python3 optimize.py --opt ... --ngrams-only                         # just build ngrams
6	    python3 optimize.py --opt ... --evaluate-only                       # re-score, no search
7	
8	WHY THIS EXISTS
9	---------------
10	The optimizer ships corpora of English prose. This layout is not typed by an
11	average English speaker; it is typed by one person writing agent prompts, shell
12	commands, Nix and Slack. freq.py already collects that corpus. This is the
13	bridge: corpus -> per-source ngram directories -> one weighted blend -> search.
14	
15	WHAT IT REPORTS, AND WHY IT IS A DELTA
16	--------------------------------------
17	An optimizer's "optimum" is unfalsifiable against a hand-designed layout: it is
18	the best point in a space defined by somebody's weights, and the weights are the
19	argument. So every run evaluates the CURRENT layout under the same config and
20	the same corpus, and the output is the comparison. A layout that wins by 2% on a
21	metric nobody has calibrated is not an instruction to re-learn your keyboard.
22	
23	WHAT MOVES AND WHAT DOES NOT
24	----------------------------
25	Thumbs never move: config/keyboard/sval.yml marks all twelve thumb switches
26	`fixed_keys: true`, so they are not in the layout string at all. That is the
27	right outcome for the reason keyboards/svalboard/README.md gives -- the thumb
28	cluster is argued from hardware the optimizer cannot model (one thumb holds one
29	key; only the knuckle+nail fat-finger pair chords; double-down is a harder press
30	of down, not a sixth position).
31	
32	On the fingers, the 26 alphas and the 7 promoted symbols float. The other six
33	printable layer-0 keys (`,` `.` `/` `;` `'` `"`) are pinned with --fix, because
34	sval.yml marks every finger key permutable and --fix is the only per-key freeze
35	that does not mean editing a config whose key costs were fitted to it.
36	
37	THE CORPUS NEVER ENTERS THIS REPO
38	---------------------------------
39	Corpus text and the ngram files derived from it are written under the optimizer
40	checkout and $CACHE, never here. A 3-gram file is not an aggregate -- it leaks
41	substrings -- and this repo is public.
42	"""

47	import re

58	# Per-cup order in config/keyboard/sval.yml: north, then the lower-x lateral,
59	# center, the higher-x lateral, south. East is screen-right on both hands, so
60	# the lower-x lateral is West on both -- which is the OUTWARD key on the left
61	# hand and the INWARD one on the right. build.py's own constants say the same
62	# thing; taking them from there rather than restating them is the point.

content.text:
**Review clean. Phase done.**

## What the retry got

Six panel iterations total. Iterations 1–4 were tooling failure, not signal — reviewers finishing without calling `submit_findings`, a seed swallowed by a herdr pane, one iteration timing out 0-of-4, and iteration 2 invalidated mid-flight because HEAD moved underneath it.

**Iterations 5 and 6 both came back clean on all four angles.** Iteration 6 reviewed `8165c97` — the exact commit on disk. I read each `implement-review-6-<angle>.json` rather than trusting the summary line:

```
correctness     clean   security   clean
error-handling  clean   type-design clean
```

Zero Critical, zero Important. The earlier gap is closed too — correctness had only ever reviewed `394dc86`, two commits stale; it has now seen `keyboard_config` and `aggregate_payload`.

## Fixed on the way

Two new commits, pushed:

- **`78dde50`** — every corpus read/write pinned to UTF-8. Rated a nit; it isn't. A program whose entire output is character counts must not have counts that depend on `LANG`. Also: `.get("messages", [])` turned any wrong-shaped dump into an empty list, so a changed search API would read as "you sent no messages" while the corpus silently shrank. And `build_ngrams`' `prefix` default duplicated `--name`'s.
- **`8165c97`** — two UTF-8 sites in `optimize.py` I'd missed (which made the previous commit message a half-truth), plus `run()`'s dead `capture` parameter.

42 tests pass, `build.py`'s four guards pass, `.vil` byte-identical, tree clean.

## Recorded, not silently dropped

Four surviving nits are deliberately deferred (the `\x00PATH:` marker having no owner; `PERMUTING` read only by tests; the scratch copy surviving a SIGKILL; `discord_plain` leaving `<t:unix:style>` markup). One correctness nit I **rejected**: `DISCORD_EMOJI`'s `\w+` was flagged for missing hyphenated emoji names, but Discord emoji names are `[A-Za-z0-9_]` only — widening it adds a branch that never fires. All of it is in the handoff with reasons.

The `<t:…>` one is worth fixing the moment a real Discord export lands, because it injects two `:` per timestamp and `:` is a promoted symbol.

**Next action (<2 min):** request the Discord export — Settings → Data & Privacy → Request all my data. Days to a month, and the loader still hasn't seen real data.

def iter_discord_text():
    """Messages you sent on Discord, from the official data export.

    NOT an API scraper, on purpose. Discord offers no ToS-clean way to read
    your own history programmatically: a user token against the API is a
    self-bot and is bannable, and a bot user can only see guilds you administer
    and never your DMs. The clean route is the export you are entitled to --
    Settings -> Data & Privacy -> Request all my data -- which takes days to a
    month to arrive. Unzip it to $CACHE/discord/ so that
    $CACHE/discord/messages/<channel>/messages.csv exists.

    Everything in that export is yours by construction, so there is no author
    filtering to do. Read with the csv module rather than by lines: Contents is
    a quoted field and multi-line messages span lines inside it.
    """
    root = DISCORD_DIR / "messages"
    if not root.is_dir():
        print(f"  discord: {root} missing, skipping "
              "(request the export: Settings -> Data & Privacy)", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    paths = sorted(root.glob("*/messages.csv"))
    n = skipped = 0
    for path in paths:
        try:
            with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
                reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
                if reader.fieldnames is None or "Contents" not in reader.fieldnames:
                    print(f"  discord: {path.parent.name} has no Contents column "
                          f"({reader.fieldnames}), skipping", file=sys.stderr)
                    continue
                for row in reader:
                    text = row.get("Contents")
                    if not text:
                        skipped += 1
                        continue
                    n += 1

def iter_discord_text():
    """Messages you sent on Discord, from the official data export.

    NOT an API scraper, on purpose. Discord offers no ToS-clean way to read
    your own history programmatically: a user token against the API is a
    self-bot and is bannable, and a bot user can only see guilds you administer
    and never your DMs. The clean route is the export you are entitled to --
    Settings -> Data & Privacy -> Request all my data -- which takes days to a
    month to arrive. Unzip it to $CACHE/discord/ so that
    $CACHE/discord/messages/<channel>/messages.csv exists.

    Everything in that export is yours by construction, so there is no author
    filtering to do. Read with the csv module rather than by lines: Contents is
    a quoted field and multi-line messages span lines inside it.
    """
    root = DISCORD_DIR / "messages"
    if not root.is_dir():
        print(f"  discord: {root} missing, skipping "
              "(request the export: Settings -> Data & Privacy)", file=sys.stderr)
        return
    paths = sorted(root.glob("*/messages.csv"))
    n = skipped = 0
    for path in paths:
        try:
            with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
                reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
                if reader.fieldnames is None or "Contents" not in reader.fieldnames:
                    print(f"  discord: {path.parent.name} has no Contents column "
                          f"({reader.fieldnames}), skipping", file=sys.stderr)
                    continue
                for row in reader:
                    text = row.get("Contents")
                    if not text:
                        skipped += 1
                        continue
                    n += 1
                    yield discord_plain(text)
        except (OSError, csv.Error) as exc:
            print(f"  discord: {path} unreadable ({exc}), skipping", file=sys.stderr)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tests for freq.py's corpus loaders.

Run: python3 keyboards/svalboard/test_freq.py

Only the loaders with a *parseable input format* are pinned here. `prompts`,
`shell` and `code` read whatever happens to be on this machine and have no
contract worth asserting; the Slack and Discord loaders read an export format
that is specified elsewhere and can silently change under us, which is exactly
the thing a test should catch.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import freq


class SlackLoaderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def with_dump(self, name: str, payload) -> Path:
        """Point freq.SLACK_DIR at a temp dir holding one dump file."""
        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        d = Path(tmp.name)
        (d / name).write_text(json.dumps(payload))
        old = freq.SLACK_DIR
        freq.SLACK_DIR = d
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))
        return d

    def test_slack_is_a_registered_source(self):
        self.assertIn("slack", freq.SOURCES)

    def test_yields_message_text_from_a_dump(self):
        self.with_dump("dump.json", [{"text": "one"}, {"text": "two"}])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["one", "two"])

    def test_missing_dump_dir_yields_nothing(self):
        old = freq.SLACK_DIR
        freq.SLACK_DIR = Path("/nonexistent/svalboard-freq-test/slack")
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), [])

    def test_html_entities_are_unescaped(self):
        # The layout argues about where `&` goes; Slack ships it as &, so
        # counting the raw text would undercount the character this repo cares
        # most about placing.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [{"text": "a & b <c> d"}])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["a & b <c> d"])

    def test_a_literally_typed_entity_survives_unescaping(self):
        # The reason slack_plain unescapes & LAST. Someone typing the four
        # characters "<" sends the wire form "&lt;". Unescape &
        # first and that collapses to "<": four keystrokes counted as one, and
        # one of them is the `&` whose rate decides where `&` goes.
        self.assertEqual(freq.slack_plain("&lt;"), "<")

    def test_mentions_and_channel_refs_are_dropped(self):
        # You autocomplete these; your hands never type the U0123ABC.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "hey <@U0123ABC> see <#C0456DEF|general> <!here>"},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["hey  see  "])

    def test_links_keep_the_label_and_drop_the_url(self):
        # A pasted URL is not typing; a label you wrote is.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "see <https://ex.com/x|the docs> and <https://ex.com/y>"},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["see the docs and "])

    def test_subtyped_and_empty_messages_are_skipped(self):
        # Joins, bot posts and file-share stubs are not keystrokes.
        self.with_dump("d.json", [
            {"text": "real"},
            {"text": "x joined", "subtype": "channel_join"},
            {"text": "beep", "subtype": "bot_message"},
            {"text": ""},
            {"no_text_key": 1},
        ])

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["real"])

    def test_a_dump_of_the_wrong_shape_says_so_instead_of_vanishing(self):
        # A dict with no "messages" key, or a bare scalar, is a dump written
        # wrong -- most likely a changed search-API response. Yielding nothing
        # silently makes that indistinguishable from "you sent no messages",
        # and the corpus just quietly shrinks. The discord loader already
        # announces this case; slack should too.
        self.with_dump("d.json", {"items": [{"text": "wrong key"}]})

        with self.assertLogs_stderr() as err:
            self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), [])
        self.assertIn("d.json", err())
        self.assertIn("shape", err())

    def assertLogs_stderr(self):
        import contextlib
        import io

        buf = io.StringIO()

        class Cap:
            def __enter__(inner):
                inner.ctx = contextlib.redirect_stderr(buf)
                inner.ctx.__enter__()
                return lambda: buf.getvalue()

            def __exit__(inner, *a):
                return inner.ctx.__exit__(*a)

        return Cap()

    def test_dumps_are_decoded_as_utf8_regardless_of_locale(self):
        # freq.py exists to count characters. Decoding the corpus through
        # whatever LANG happens to be set would make the counts themselves
        # machine-dependent -- the one thing this tool must not be.
        import tempfile

        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        d = Path(tmp.name)
        (d / "d.json").write_bytes(
            json.dumps([{"text": "café — naïve"}], ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
        )
        old = freq.SLACK_DIR
        freq.SLACK_DIR = d
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["café — naïve"])

    def test_accepts_the_messages_envelope_form(self):
        # slack_search_* returns {"messages": [...]}; a hand-saved dump may be
        # the bare list. Both are dumps we would plausibly write.
        self.with_dump("d.json", {"messages": [{"text": "enveloped"}]})

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["enveloped"])


class DiscordLoaderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def with_export(self, *channels: tuple[str, str]) -> Path:
        """Point freq.DISCORD_DIR at a temp export root.

        Each channel is (dir_name, raw messages.csv text) -- raw, because the
        CSV quoting is half of what this loader has to get right.
        """
        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        root = Path(tmp.name)
        for name, csv_text in channels:
            d = root / "messages" / name
            d.mkdir(parents=True)
            (d / "messages.csv").write_text(csv_text)
        old = freq.DISCORD_DIR
        freq.DISCORD_DIR = root
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "DISCORD_DIR", old))
        return root

    def test_discord_is_a_registered_source(self):
        self.assertIn("discord", freq.SOURCES)

    def test_yields_contents_across_channels(self):
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,hello,\n2,t,there,\n'),
            ("c2", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n3,t,again,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["hello", "there", "again"])

    def test_missing_export_yields_nothing(self):
        old = freq.DISCORD_DIR
        freq.DISCORD_DIR = Path("/nonexistent/svalboard-freq-test/discord")
        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "DISCORD_DIR", old))

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), [])

    def test_multiline_messages_survive_csv_quoting(self):
        # The reason this reads CSV properly instead of splitting on newlines:
        # a quoted Contents field spans lines, and naive splitting would shred
        # every multi-line message into fragments.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,"one\ntwo",\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["one\ntwo"])

    def test_mentions_dropped_and_custom_emoji_reduced_to_typed_form(self):
        self.with_export((
            "c1",
            'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n'
            '1,t,"hey <@123> and <@!456> in <#789> role <@&321> emoji <:party:1> <a:spin:2>",\n',
        ))

        self.assertEqual(
            list(freq.iter_discord_text()),
            ["hey  and  in  role  emoji :party: :spin:"],
        )

    def test_empty_contents_rows_are_skipped(self):
        # Attachment-only messages: a drag-and-drop, not keystrokes.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n1,t,,https://cdn/x.png\n2,t,real,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["real"])

    def test_unexpected_columns_skip_the_file_without_crashing(self):
        # Discord has changed this export's shape before; a silent zero-count
        # is worse than a loud skip.
        self.with_export(
            ("c1", 'ID,Timestamp,Body\n1,t,hello\n'),
            ("c2", 'ID,Timestamp,Contents,Attachments\n2,t,fine,\n'),
        )

        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_discord_text()), ["fine"])


class AggregateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_source_that_collected_nothing_is_omitted_not_zero_filled(self):
        # freq.json is the public evidence base the README's placement argument
        # rests on. A source with no corpus emitted as a full table of 0.0
        # reads as "measured, never typed" -- the strongest possible claim --
        # when it means "never measured". discord is exactly this until the
        # export lands.
        payload = freq.aggregate_payload({"shell": "abc", "discord": ""})

        self.assertEqual(set(payload["corpus_chars"]), {"shell"})
        self.assertEqual(set(payload["rates"]), {"shell"})

    def test_a_source_with_a_corpus_is_reported(self):
        payload = freq.aggregate_payload({"shell": "a-b-c"})

        self.assertEqual(payload["corpus_chars"]["shell"], 5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(payload["rates"]["shell"]["-"], 400.0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def emoji_shortcode(match):
    """A literal emoji back to roughly the `:name:` that produced it.

    The name is unicodedata's, so it approximates Discord's shortcode rather
    than reproducing it (`:thinking_face:`, where Discord says `:thinking:`).

def emoji_shortcode(match):
    """A run of literal emoji back to the keys that produced it.

    Emoji go in as `:eye<tab>`, not as `:eyes:` -- you type a colon, enough
    letters to disambiguate, and Tab. The closing colon and the rest of the
    name come from the autocomplete, so reconstructing the rendered name would
    invent a second colon and a word nobody's hands made. This models the
    keystrokes: one `:`, EMOJI_PREFIX letters, one Tab.

    The prefix length is a stand-in for "enough to disambiguate" and is the
    approximate part; the colon count, which is what the layout argument turns
    on, is exact. The trailing Tab also makes a fabricated `::` structurally
    impossible between adjacent emoji -- and a same-key repeat on a lateral is
    the exact signal the `-` finding rests on.
    """
    out = []
    for ch in match.group():
        name = unicodedata.name(ch, "")
        if name:
            letters = "".join(c for c in name.lower() if c.isalpha())
            out.append(f":{letters[:EMOJI_PREFIX]}\t")
    return "".join(out)

**On hotkeys: I'd skip them, and the reason is structural, not effort.** Thumbs are `fixed_keys: true` in the optimizer config and aren't in the 40-char layout string at all. svalboard: read the Discord export that actually arrived, and count emoji as keystrokes

The export landed and it is not the shape the loader was written for. There is
no CSV in it at all: 1085 channels, every one messages.json, under a
capitalised Messages/. Same field names, different container. Both shapes are
read now, and the directory is matched case-insensitively, so an older export
sitting in $CACHE is not stranded.

It is also, at 7.4M characters over 339,675 messages, the largest corpus here
-- bigger than the prompt transcripts. That made the 0.05 weight it carried
while missing indefensible. It is 0.20 now, then rebalanced again with code
dropped to 0.08: Sauyon does not hand-write much code any more, and the typing
that replaced it is in `prompts`.

Emoji are the interesting part. Discord stores the RENDERED character for
standard emoji, so nothing of what was pressed survives: 15,673 of them
against 11,239 surviving colons, which took `:` -- one of the seven symbols
README.md promoted on a measured rate -- down by ~2.4x. What actually gets
typed is `:eye<tab>`: one colon, a short prefix, Tab. The closing colon and
the rest of the name are the autocomplete's, so reconstructing `:eyes:` would
invent a colon and a word nobody's hands made. Modelling the keystrokes
instead put discord's `:` at 3.59/1k, up from 1.52.

The Tab is not cosmetic either: it makes a fabricated `::` structurally
impossible between adjacent emoji, and a same-key repeat on a lateral is the
exact signal the `-` finding rests on.

Also dropped, as things nobody types: bare pasted URLs (slack_plain already
did this) and `<t:1681414200:t>` timestamps, which Discord inserts and which
carry two colons each.

Known and not fixed: Slack's API returns shortcodes as literal `:eyes:` text,
so slack over-counts `:` by its 14 shortcodes -- noise in a 15k corpus at
weight 0.10, against Discord's ~27k colons.

None of it moved the result: current layout 838.11 against 838.22 before the
emoji fix, and the ranking is unchanged. That is the point of recording it.

48 tests (28 freq, 22 optimize... 20 -> 28 as the export shape and the emoji
model each earned their own).

2	"""Tests for freq.py's corpus loaders.
3	
4	Run: python3 keyboards/svalboard/test_freq.py
5	
6	Only the loaders with a *parseable input format* are pinned here. `prompts`,
7	`shell` and `code` read whatever happens to be on this machine and have no
8	contract worth asserting; the Slack and Discord loaders read an export format
9	that is specified elsewhere and can silently change under us, which is exactly
10	the thing a test should catch.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import json
16	import tempfile
17	import unittest
18	from pathlib import Path
19	
20	import freq
21	
22	
23	class SlackLoaderTests(unittest.TestCase):
24	    def with_dump(self, name: str, payload) -> Path:
25	        """Point freq.SLACK_DIR at a temp dir holding one dump file."""
26	        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
27	        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
28	        d = Path(tmp.name)
29	        (d / name).write_text(json.dumps(payload))
30	        old = freq.SLACK_DIR
31	        freq.SLACK_DIR = d
32	        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))
33	        return d
34	
35	    def test_slack_is_a_registered_source(self):
36	        self.assertIn("slack", freq.SOURCES)
37	
38	    def test_yields_message_text_from_a_dump(self):
39	        self.with_dump("dump.json", [{"text": "one"}, {"text": "two"}])
40	
41	        self.assertEqual(list(freq.iter_slack_text()), ["one", "two"])

46	        self.addCleanup(lambda: setattr(freq, "SLACK_DIR", old))

52	        # counting the raw text would undercount the character this repo cares

svalboard: read the Discord export that actually arrived, and count emoji as keystrokes

The export landed and it is not the shape the loader was written for. There is
no CSV in it at all: 1085 channels, every one messages.json, under a
capitalised Messages/. Same field names, different container. Both shapes are
read now and the directory is matched case-insensitively, so an older export in
$CACHE is not stranded -- one file per channel, JSON preferred, because reading
both would have counted a channel holding both twice and that would have been
invisible in the rates.

It is also, at 7.4M characters over 339,669 messages, the largest corpus here
-- bigger than the prompt transcripts. That made the 0.05 weight it carried
while missing indefensible. Weights are now prompts .38 / discord .26 /
shell .18 / slack .10 / code .08, code low because Sauyon does not hand-write
much any more and the typing that replaced it is in `prompts`.

Emoji are the interesting part. Discord stores the RENDERED character for
standard emoji, so nothing of what was pressed survives: 15,673 of them against
11,239 surviving colons, taking `:` -- one of the seven symbols README.md
promoted on a measured rate -- down by ~2.4x. What actually gets typed is
`:eye<tab>`: one colon, a short prefix, Tab. The closing colon and the rest of
the name are the autocomplete's, so reconstructing `:eyes:` would invent a
colon and a word nobody's hands made. Modelling the keystrokes put discord's
`:` at 3.59/1k, up from 1.52.

The Tab is not cosmetic: it makes a fabricated `::` structurally impossible
between adjacent emoji, and a same-key repeat on a lateral is the exact signal
the `-` finding rests on.

Also dropped as things nobody types: bare pasted URLs (slack_plain already did
this), and `<t:...>` timestamps, which Discord inserts and which carry two
colons each. URLs are stripped BEFORE emoji restoration -- restoration inserts
a Tab and the URL pattern stops at whitespace, so the other order cut links in
half and counted the tail.

Test fixtures are invented text and invented ids, not lines from the export.
The rule this whole pipeline is built around is that the corpus never lands in
this public repo, and a fixture is still in it.

Known and not fixed: Slack's API returns shortcodes as literal `:eyes:`, so
slack over-counts `:` by its 14 shortcodes -- noise in a 15k corpus at weight
.10 against Discord's ~27k colons.

None of it moved the result: current layout 838.11 against 838.22 before, and
the ranking is unchanged. That is why it is worth recording.

52 tests (30 freq, 22 optimize).

content.text:
Pushed, review clean, tree clean.

## The export was not the shape the loader expected

Three things were wrong, all found by running against real data:

- **No CSV at all.** 1,085 channels, every one `messages.json`, under a capitalised `Messages/`. Field names identical, container changed. Both shapes read now, directory matched case-insensitively.
- **Double-count bug** (review, Important): reading both shapes counted a channel holding both twice. Nothing was actually double-counted — but it was one stale file from firing, invisibly.
- **URL/emoji ordering**: emoji restoration inserts a Tab, and the URL pattern stops at whitespace, so an emoji inside a link cut it in half and counted the tail.

## Your `:eye<tab>` correction was the important one

Discord stores the *rendered* character, so nothing you pressed survives: **15,673 emoji against 11,239 surviving colons**. I'd first reconstructed `:eyes:` — which would have invented a second colon and a word your hands never made. Modelling the actual keystrokes (`:` + prefix + Tab) put Discord's `:` at **3.59/1k, up from 1.52**.

The Tab isn't cosmetic: it makes a fabricated `::` impossible between adjacent emoji, and a same-key repeat on a lateral is exactly the signal the `-` finding rests on.

Review then caught me over-correcting: 👍🏽 and ZWJ families are multiple codepoints, so one autocomplete was emitting two or three colons. Fixed to match whole clusters.

**I also had to rewrite history.** I'd put real message text, IDs and timestamps from your export into a test fixture — in a public repo, violating the one non-negotiable of this whole run. It was caught before the push; the two commits were rewritten with invented fixtures, so it never reached `forge.ko.ag`.

## None of it moved the answer

| | current | best candidate |
|---|---|---|
| before Discord | 1035.60 | 216.03 |
| + Discord, code 0.17 | 860.68 | 245.95 |
| code → 0.08 | 838.22 | 242.86 |
| + emoji correction | 838.11 | 242.41 |

Weights as you chose: prompts .38 / discord .26 / shell .18 / slack .10 / code .08.

The `-` finding is **weight-independent** — it's doubled in every corpus separately: shell 35.1%, code 37.2%, prompts 25.4%, Discord 16.0%.

One thing Discord did change: **`~` is 85.9% doubled there** (`~~strikethrough~~`), against 0% in shell. The README put `~` on a ring lateral precisely because it measured "zero consecutive repeats" — true for its corpus, false once personal chat is in. That argument now cuts both ways.

**Next action (<2 min):** `git log --oneline -3` to see what landed, or say the word and I'll run the three weightings side by side to separate the weight-independent findings from the artifacts.
